actions.description: Command one or more actuated joints to target positions in joint space, optionally over a declared duration, and report whether the target was reached within tolerance.

inputs.description: Target angle of joints 1 to 6, in rad

limit.reason: set_servo_angle documents its angle as 0-180 degrees (line 462) and clamps the converted position to 1024-3072; 0-180 degrees is 0-pi rad

inputs.name: joint_positions

actions.name: move_joints

actions.description: Drive axes to their declared home position or reference switch, establishing the coordinate reference needed by other motion capabilities.

inputs.description: Fraction of the upstream 0-32767 moving-speed range; omit it for go_home's default
inputs.name: speed_scale

actions.name: home

actions.description: Disable the torque of servos 1 to 6 (the safe state); it takes no input
actions.name: disable_all_torque

outputs.description: True once the torque of all six servos was disabled
outputs.name: disabled

actions.description: Re-enable the torque of servos 1 to 6 after a safety reset (the declared re-enable); it takes no input, is refused while the e-stop is latched and is never run by the reset. The upstream arm_tighten documents that the arm then holds its current position; treat it as an actuation
actions.name: enable_all_torque

outputs.description: True once the torque of all six servos was enabled
outputs.name: enabled

facts.text: The application runs simulations and controls a Bambot and an SO100 arm
The application controls real robot arms with Feetech SCS servo motors whose IDs are 1 to 6
The servo IDs are configured from 1 to 6 matching the joint numbers, the bus runs at a fixed 1,000,000 bps and the protocol is SCS (1)
The controller's constructor defaults are port COM4, 1,000,000 baud and a 0.1 s timeout
The serial port is opened with eight data bits, no parity and one stop bit (8N1)
Every SCS packet starts with two 0xFF bytes and carries the servo ID, the length, the instruction, its parameters and a one-byte checksum
set_servo_angle accepts an angle of 0-180 degrees, converts it to the 1024-3072 position range and clamps it there
A moving speed is 0-32767 and a speed of 0 means the highest speed
read_position returns the present-position register value, documented as 0-4095
get_servo_angle converts the 1024-3072 present position back to 0-180 degrees
enable_torque writes 1 and disable_torque writes 0 to the torque-enable register
sync_disable_torque writes 0 to the torque-enable register of every named servo and falls back to disable_torque one servo at a time when the sync write fails
sync_enable_torque writes 1 to the torque-enable register of every named servo and falls back to enable_torque one servo at a time when the sync write fails
The upstream MCP tool arm_tighten enables the torque of servos 1 to 6 with sync_enable_torque and documents that the arm then holds its current position
go_home moves servos 1 to 6 to 90, 0, 180, 180, 90 and 90 degrees; the comment on servo 4 says 0 but the code writes 180
read_position returns None when the command send or the reply fails
_write_register returns False when the command send or the reply fails

measures.description: Present angle of servos 1 to 6, in rad (0 to pi is the upstream's 0-180 degrees)
measures.name: joint_positions

operator_required.name: home
operator_required.reason: the catalogue class defines only a dimensionless 0..1 fraction and the clone states no speed-scale range for the arm; the site sets the allowed fraction

safe_state.description: torque disabled on servos 1 to 6, so the arm is limp; a reset leaves it off until the declared re-enable x-cap.itheima1.enable_all_torque.v1 turns it back on
